definitions.explanation: To insert or put something into a space or opening.

definitions.gloss: to bring refreshments or gifts (to someone working)
definitions.explanation: To bring food, drinks, or gifts to people who are working hard or to someone in detention. The noun form {差|さ}し{入|い}れ is commonly used.

examples.japanese: {鍵|かぎ}を{鍵穴|かぎあな}に{差|さ}し{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Insert the key into the keyhole.

examples.japanese: {手紙|てがみ}を{封筒|ふうとう}に{差|さ}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I slipped the letter into the envelope.

examples.japanese: コインを{自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}に{差|さ}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I inserted a coin into the vending machine.

examples.japanese: {残業|ざんぎょう}している{同僚|どうりょう}に{差|さ}し{入|い}れをした。
examples.english: I brought refreshments to my colleagues working overtime.

examples.japanese: {留置場|りゅうちじょう}にいる{友人|ゆうじん}に{本|ほん}を{差|さ}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I brought books to my friend in detention.

examples.japanese: {部活|ぶかつ}の{練習|れんしゅう}に{差|さ}し{入|い}れとしてジュースを{持|も}って{行|い}った。
examples.english: I brought juice as refreshments to the club practice.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive).

COMPOUND VERB: Formed from {差|さ}す (to insert/extend) + {入|い}れる (to put in).

NOUN FORM: {差|さ}し{入|い}れ is commonly used as a noun meaning 'refreshments/gifts brought to someone' or 'the act of bringing such items.'

CULTURAL NOTE: Bringing {差|さ}し{入|い}れ to people working hard (such as during overtime, sports practice, or moving) is a common Japanese custom showing care and appreciation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{差|さ}し{入|い}れを{持|も}って{行|い}く (bring refreshments)
・おやつを{差|さ}し{入|い}れる (bring snacks)
・{差|さ}し{入|い}れをもらう (receive refreshments)
